_doc: One entry per deviation shape. Lifecycle and gating rules: docs/GATING.md. Never delete entries; never flip still_reproduces without a fresh verifying scan. `signal` is a `|`-joined list of canonical names — each token is either a bias-report metric (docs/bias_data.json `metrics`) or a registry signal key (LANGUAGE_DEFINITIONS rules, via tools/_registry.py); no prose, no `+`, no `(various)`; tokens are sorted and unique. The reports join `signal` x `languages_seen` as a cross-product to decide whether a cell is accounted for (docs/GATING.md n/a rule 2 today; red cells from gitgalaxy#2669 E.1), so a token must hold for EVERY language listed — scope a collective entry down rather than let it excuse a cell nobody looked at. An entry that explains no cell (a workflow or classification fact) carries an empty `signal`, which never matches. `languages_seen` may be the sentinel ["all"].

entries.verdict: galaxyscope.py ~2145 ('THE CONTEXTUAL BASELINE FIX'): a file imported by others (popularity > 0) has orphaned_logic converted into api before recording. Micro-repro: 2-def file imported by a sibling records api=4, un-imported records api=2. With the spec's main->a->b->c chain and uncalled probes, api = defs x 2 in a/b/c, defs in main. Deliberate scoring semantics; raw counts unrecoverable from the DB (filed squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2536 asking for raw recording). apex added 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.3): it had no import chain at all until Type.forName('a'/'b'/'c') was planted, so a/b/c had popularity 0 and api 0; with the chain live their 3 uncalled probes convert to api 3 each, exactly this shape.

Keywords inside one string literal ('if eval fails, try open') count toward branch (+2), safety (+1), io (+1) but eval does NOT count toward high_risk_execution (routes to sec_tainted_injection instead). Micro-repro: identical files differing only in literal content, scanned end-to-end. Comments are fully stripped (verified 0 contribution); strings are inconsistently half-counted. 2026-08-31 cross-language extension: javascript reproduces python exactly (same decoy sentence, if/try count, eval does not); cobol does NOT shield at all (ALTER counts high_risk_execution from inside a DISPLAY literal) — the shielding is lexical-family-dependent, i.e. itself a language bias. 2026-08-31 legacy batch: fortran/ada/assembly count literals like cobol (fortran IF+GOTO+OPEN all count; ada 'if' counts; asm jmp/syscall count, and ARM's single-letter 'b' mnemonic even matches the filename inside %include "b.asm"); abap is a THIRD profile — shields branch/high_risk/io but NOT safety (TRY in a literal counts safety, isolated by micro-repro with comment-only vs string-only files). Worst amplification: a branch keyword inside a literal creates phantom branch context that triples state_mutation via the flux weighting (see state-flux-branch-weighting). Current behavior baked into manifests; whether intentional is the upstream question. 2026-08-31 batch 3 (12 mainstream languages): the selective profile (high-risk family shielded, branch/safety/io count) holds for c/cpp/csharp/java/go/kotlin/typescript/php/lua/swift; ruby counts eval from the literal (eval-as-bypass, like shell); perl's eval survives only because its bypass rule requires eval-followed-by-quote/paren (syntax shielding, not surface shielding); swift's api rule counts the word 'open' inside the literal (API-exposure mass from prose). try counts branch in csharp/java/kotlin/php/perl/swift/typescript. Swift's bare-open api FP filed as squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2544. 2026-08-31 batch 4 (Tier-1 completion): a FOURTH profile — scheme's sexp-anchored branch keywords shield strings by SYNTAX (bare 'if' in a literal cannot match the paren-anchored rule) while its unanchored eval still counts; m4 is fully inert by the same mechanism (macro-name keywords). matlab and tcl join shell/ruby in counting eval-as-bypass from literals. dockerfile/makefile/livecode count literals wholesale. swift-open-style api hit not repeated elsewhere. RESOLVED-AS-EXPLAINED 2026-09-01: gitgalaxy#2535 closed as not-a-bug after root-cause isolation. There is NO string-literal shielding mechanism anywhere in the engine -- strings are never stripped/masked from the code stream for any structural signal, in any language (only comments are). Every observed 'shielding' shape here is the ordinary Silencer Region dampener (spatial_correlation.py apply_dampener_correlations Block 2: high_risk_execution <- safety, 500-char radius) firing because the shared decoy sentence 'if eval fails, try open' happens to contain both a real danger keyword AND a real safety keyword for SOME languages, by accident of English-word/rule-vocabulary overlap -- not a deliberate per-language shielding design. Isolated via direct micro-repro: python state_danger 0->1 the instant 'try' is swapped out of the decoy with nothing else changed. Per-language explanation for the profiles recorded above: python/js/haskell/abap ('shielded'/'inverted') all have TRY (or their language's equivalent) in their OWN safety rule, so the dampener fires; cobol/fortran/ada/assembly ('unshielded') do NOT have TRY in their safety rule (cobol's is END-IF/END-PERFORM/.../VALIDATE/CHECK), so it never fires; rust's 'shielded' reading was actually a THIRD, unrelated cause -- its high_risk_execution rule has no 'eval' concept at all (panic!/todo!/process::exit), a morphology mismatch, not shielding. The #2546 'phantom branch trigger from string literals' shares this exact explanation (no shielding exists, so a genuinely-present branch keyword correctly triggers the flux dampener regardless of surface). Follow-up filed as a CORPUS issue (decoy sentence design), not an engine issue -- see keyword-rosetta issue tracking decoy redesign. capstones jcl.md/cobol.md/python.md corrected to match. DECOY REDESIGN PILOT 2026-09-01 (keyword-rosetta#17): python/fortran/rust re-authored to a danger-only literal ('plain eval|ASSIGN|abort decoy text') per the redesigned SPEC §String decoy. All three profiles converge on the same clean read -- the danger keyword counts +1 from inside the literal, undampened: python eval +1 (was 0 under the old sentence's try-collision), fortran ASSIGN +1 (GOTO retired from the decoy: it doubles as a branch keyword and fed the x3 flux -- state_mutation 6->2), rust abort +1 (the first time rust's decoy tested anything; eval matches nothing in its danger rule; state 6->2). One new engine fact surfaced by the pilot and now recorded in SPEC: dampener correlations are function-scoped, but MODULE-LEVEL code falls back to flat 500-char-radius behavior (apply_dampener_correlations docstring) -- python's literal initially read 0 at module level because probe_safety's assert sat ~450 chars away; moving it inside probe_globals isolated it. DECOY REDESIGN COMPLETE 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.1 wave 2, 32 languages; A.3 wave 3, abap/assembly/cobol/sqlite): all 40 languages_seen now carry a danger-only literal, gates green. Screening rule that made it mechanical: run the candidate literal through the language's live compiled rules and require exactly one high_risk_execution hit and zero hits in any SCORED column -- the planted set plus the seven non-planted signals that feed a risk_* formula (_registry.risk_dependencies(): concurrency, sync_locks, reflection_metaprogramming, immutability_locks, spec_exposure, debug_prints, llm_api). That rejected Thread.Abort (csharp), Thread.stop (java) and iex (powershell), each clean against the planted set alone. Filler words need the same check: 'text' matches dart's and embedded_python's ui_framework rule. Findings from the sweep: matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval under safety_bypasses, NOT high_risk_execution, so their old decoy exercised the wrong family (safety_bypasses 3->2 each); swift's api rule counted the prose 'open' (api 4->3, a scored planted column fed from inside a string, the #2544 shape); abap's recorded 'third profile' was the Silencer Region after all -- dropping TRY takes its TRUNCATE 0->1; scheme moved no count at all, its sexp-anchored branch rule never having matched the prose 'if'; assembly keeps its x3 flux because probe_state's own 'ret' is a branch keyword, unlike the 35 languages where the retired 'if' was the only branch in scope. sqlite needs a two-word literal ('DROP DATABASE') -- its danger vocabulary has no single bare token. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the field now names every column this shape moves, not just the headline four — state_mutation (the x3 flux amplification), safety_bypasses (matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval there, not under high_risk_execution) and api (swift's rule counting the prose 'open', #2544) are consequences recorded in the verdict above and are joined on here.

python's test rule includes \bassert\b and the safety rule includes assert: one planted assert counts both. Legitimate overlapping taxonomies; record +1 test wherever a safety assert is planted. Also c (bare assert( in both rules) and perl (ok( in the test rule alongside croak/confess safety plants). RESOLVED for python via gitgalaxy #2626 (assert removed from the test rule, still matched by safety): a.py test dropped 3->2. Still reproduces for c/perl (their own rule files are unchanged).

python-family io rule matches the os./sys. prefixes that the globals plants (os.environ, sys.argv) necessarily carry: +2 io in whichever file hosts probe_globals. RESOLVED for python via gitgalaxy #2626 (io rule gained negative lookaheads excluding os.environ/sys.argv from the io match): a.py io dropped 3->1. No other language currently in languages_seen.

Debt rules are whole-text, not comment-anchored, and '-' is a regex word boundary: HACK-LEVEL (data item, 2 code occurrences) counts fragile_debt, PROBE-TODO (paragraph name) counts planned_debt. Python's HACK_LEVEL is inert only because '_' is a word character — tokenization luck, not surface anchoring. Real-world FP shapes: COBOL BUG-COUNT/WS-FIX-FLAG, css .bug-icon, lisp fix-me. Filed upstream; observed counts baked into cobol manifest until fixed. Batch 4: scheme reproduces it — (define (probe-todo ...)) records planned_debt 2 (comment + identifier), confirming the lisp-family exposure predicted in #2537. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2622 (closes #2537) — hyphenated-identifier guards ((?<![A-Za-z0-9]-) / (?!-[A-Za-z0-9])) on the shared GLOBAL_FRAGILE_DEBT/GLOBAL_PLANNED_DEBT patterns. Fresh verifying scan (engine at PR #2622 head): cobol c.cpy fragile_debt 3->1, planned_debt 2->1; scheme c.scm planned_debt 2->1 — only the planted * HACK: / * TODO: / ;; TODO: comments count. Real comment markers incl. the hyphen-adjacent family (-- TODO, --TODO, TODO--) verified still counting via the upstream PR's strict tests. Manifests re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4.

A bare token + period in Area B (CEE3DMP. / CEEMOUT., column 12) is counted as a paragraph header: func_start regex's post-sequence-area [ \t]* tolerates any indentation (relaxed/free-format support). By strict reference format a paragraph-name must start in Area A. b.cpy records func_start 5 (3 real paragraphs + 2). Whether the relaxed tolerance is deliberate is the upstream question. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2552 (closes #2538 -- func_start no longer mistakes LE service calls for paragraphs). Fresh verifying scan (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2552/#2611): b.cpy func_start 5->3, api 5->3 (orphan conversion follows), telemetry/safety_bypasses/state_mutation unchanged at 2/2/2 -- only the two bare-token FPs vanished. Manifest re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4. Surfaced by the first all-language CI run since #2552 merged (rosetta PR #5, which touches no data/ so the gate ran all 46).

'with (shape) {}' is parsed as a function named 'with' by the identifier(args){ alternation: the keyword exclusion list has if/for/while/switch/catch/return but not with. finditer-confirmed; switch (flag) {} in the same corpus is correctly excluded. b.js records func_start/args 4 for 3 functions. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2539 ('with' added to the func_start/args statement-keyword exclusions, JS and TS): b.js func_start/args/api 4->3.

cobol globals pattern includes WORKING-STORAGE\s+SECTION as an alternative — every fixed-format program with a working-storage section records globals >= 1. keyword_menu.py missed it (multi-word alternation; the miner only validates single-token candidates) — menu-tool improvement noted. main.cbl globals 1 baked in.

Token signals match ordinary identifiers that happen to spell a keyword: js probeIo's parameter named 'path' counts io +1 (path is a js io keyword). Inherent to keyword-based signals. Authoring guidance: avoid naming identifiers after menu keywords unless the collision is the point; record it when unavoidable. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): narrowed from the prose '(any token signal)' to `io`, the one collision actually verified (javascript probeIo's `path` parameter). The shape generalises but the ledger must not claim to explain a cell nobody has looked at; a new collision is a new occurrence, added when observed.

state_mutation is recorded x3 when branch context exists in the file ('flux' semantics, matching the state_flux column name). Micro-repro: one := inside a real ada if -> 3; one := with no branch -> 1; the multiplier applies file-wide to all mutations. python/cobol corpus files were exact only because their b files had no branch context. Consequence of #2535: a branch keyword inside a string literal creates PHANTOM branch context and triples unrelated real mutations ('while' in a string: 2 raw := -> 6). REFINED (batch 3, go micro-evidence): the x3 weighting is PER-FUNCTION, not per-file — go b.go records 11 = probe_state's 3 raw x3 (its own string carries the branch keyword) + probe_bypass's 2 raw x1 (no branch context in that function). Reproduces in all 12 batch-3 languages whose state rules have raw hits alongside the string decoy. Batch 4 adds the three cleanest per-function proofs: matlab main = 12 = one function's 3 raw x3 + three functions' 1 raw x1; powershell c stays x1 because probe_debt has no return/branch while its sibling does; dockerfile scopes flux per RUN instruction (4 = 1x3 + 1x1). DOCUMENTED 2026-09-01: gitgalaxy PR #2631 (closes #2546) resolves the upstream question as deliberate design, kept and now documented + test-pinned. SEMANTICS CORRECTION to this entry's earlier description: the x3 is a 150-CHARACTER proximity radius per mutation within the same function (spatial_correlation.py Block 6, correlate_scoped) -- NOT a blanket per-function branch-context toggle; corpus probe functions were simply shorter than the radius, which masked the distinction (the per-function refinement was correct about scoping, wrong about the trigger being function-wide). Raw counts are recoverable as recorded - 2*amplified_cascading_flux (per-file mitigation_telemetry, audit report 'Contextual Mitigations & Amplifications'). Behavior unchanged, so still_reproduces stays true; the actionable blocker for the corpus's state_mutation median inflation is now #2535 ALONE (the phantom literal trigger) -- language tracking issues' state_mutation residuals re-point there. 2026-09-01 (gitgalaxy#2634 / #2545 landing): this entry's powershell `c` evidence line no longer discriminates — with `return` out of `branch`, probe_todo has no branch context either, so powershell c is x1 throughout and c branch is 0. The go / matlab / dockerfile per-function proofs are untouched and remain this entry's evidence. Same landing removes the phantom `return` context that was tripling apex c.cls (state_mutation 3 -> 1, re-baselined with it): a real reduction in flux inflation, not a semantics change.

'USE A' does not resolve to a.f90 in the dependency DAG (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires); 'USE a' resolves. Fortran is case-insensitive, the suffix-map lookup is not. Corpus lowercased its USE targets to keep the DAG probe live; real uppercase legacy fortran (very common) silently loses its dependency graph. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2540 (per-language case-folded fallback in the DAG suffix-map lookup for fortran/cobol/haskell, scoped to the importing language's own files): uppercase 'USE A' now resolves; corpus values unchanged (targets were lowercased as the workaround). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): scoped to `popularity|api` — the two the verdict actually pins (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires). The corpus never showed the wider graph family deviating because the USE targets were lowercased as the workaround.

ada's closing 'end if' re-matches \bif\b: every well-formed if statement counts branch at least twice (if + end if). Same class would apply to fortran 'END IF' spelled with a space (corpus used ENDIF, which is inert). Inherent to token-based branch counting on block-closed languages; baked in (main.adb branch 4).
GOTO is in both fortran's branch rule and its high_risk_execution rule — one planted GOTO counts both. finditer-confirmed.

assembly's branch rule includes call and ret (all control transfers) — correct for asm morphology but it means every probe body's ret and every glue call counts branch (main.asm: 10 = 3 call + 4 ret + 3 planted jumps). Cross-language branch comparisons must expect asm to run structurally hot.

ARM's single-letter 'b' branch mnemonic matches the word b anywhere literals count — including the filename inside %include "b.asm" (a.asm branch +1, finditer-confirmed). Any asm file mentioning a bare 'b' in a string/path gains branch mass. Sub-case of #2535's literal counting; not filed separately.

Top-level value bindings (CAFs like 'region = unsafePerformIO ...') count func_start/args like any function binding — morphologically correct for haskell, where top-level values ARE nullary functions. a.hs records 5 (3 probes + 2 planted globals). Type-signature + binding pairs count once, not twice (verified).
finally is in both haskell's cleanup and safety rules (finditer-confirmed on c.hs) — one planted finally counts both.

shell's branch rule counts the test brackets [ and ] as branch tokens (finditer on main.sh: if,[,],then,fi = 5 for one conditional) — every bracketed test costs +2 branch on top of if/then/fi. Defensible ([ is the test builtin) but a strong per-language inflation for cross-language branch comparisons.

'trap : TERM' counts globals: the TERM signal name collides with the TERM env-var keyword in shell's globals rule (a.sh globals 3 for 2 planted). Any trap handler naming TERM/USER-adjacent signals inherits this.

On languages without a same-file call graph the orphan census includes non-function shapes, so the orphan->api conversion count diverges from visible function counts: shell a/b convert 4 with 3 functions (the extra tracks the source line), sqlite converts 2/4/3 with 3 CREATE INDEX each and main.sql records orphaned_logic 7 for 4 indexes. Recorded as observed; gitgalaxy#2536 (raw hit_vector recording) would make these auditable. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2618 (closes #2547 -- synthetic slicer bucket names excluded from the orphan/duplicate census). Fresh verifying scans (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2618): the inflating orphans were the synthetic buckets themselves -- __global_context__ in livecode/lua/matlab/ruby/shell a- AND b-files (api -1 each; lua a 9->8, b 10->9), and sqlite b.sql/c.sql whose 'functions' are ALL synthetic names (CREATE_Statement/SELECT_Statement/UPDATE_Statement/Declarative_Block), so every conversion there vanishes (a.sql 2->0, b.sql 4->0, c.sql 3->0). Real probe functions unaffected everywhere; 13 manifest cells re-baselined in this change per GATING step 4. lua/ruby added to languages_seen (same __global_context__ shape, confirmed). dockerfile/powershell manifests needed no change (their counts never included the bucket). First live catch of the #2557 rosetta-audit system (run locally against pull/2618/head pre-merge).
^.read counts BOTH import and io (finditer-confirmed) — every corpus chain link adds +1 io in sqlite. By design (a .read is file io), but a cross-language io comparison must expect it.

GalaxyScope's census enumerates git-tracked files only; an untracked folder scans as '0 files mapped' with no per-file warning. Authoring workflow requires commit-before-verify (SPEC.md). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): `signal` is deliberately EMPTY. This is a workflow fact, not an explanation for any cell — an untracked folder produces no numbers at all — and an empty signal never matches the metric x language join, so it can never excuse a deviation.

The <?php open tag's ? matches php's branch rule bare ternary-? alternation (finditer-confirmed): EVERY php file records branch >= 1 from its own open tag. A systematic per-file +1 on all real-world PHP; worth an upstream look at excluding ?> / <? tag context from the ? alternation. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2541 (tag context excluded from the ternary-? alternation via (?<!<)?(?!>) guards): per-file tag +1 gone, corpus php branch main 4->3, a/c 1->0, b 3->2.

kotlin's branch rule counts return: every file's branch = returns + real branch keywords (main.kt 8 = 5 returns + if/else/when; files with only returns record branch 3). Same cross-language-inflation class as assembly's call/ret. Batch 4: apex, objective-c, powershell, and zig (pattern-confirmed) also count return — it is a 5-language family, not a kotlin quirk; scala/dart/groovy siblings do not. Strengthens #2545's inconsistency framing. Batch 5: solidity is the 6th member (main branch 8 = 5 returns + 3 keywords). RESOLVED 2026-09-01: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy#2545 (PR #2634). Checked 11 close siblings across every relevant family (java/c/rust/go/csharp/scala/dart/groovy/swift/typescript/cpp) -- none count bare return as branch, including rust/csharp which share kotlin/zig's exact early-return idiom; no defensible rationale found for any of the 6. Fix split by whether return was already tracked elsewhere: kotlin/apex/powershell/zig had it duplicated under structural_boundaries already (pure de-dup); objective-c/solidity had no other rule tracking it, so return moved there instead of being deleted (signal preserved, same convention). Re-verified against engine pull/2634/head: all 6 gates PASS, branch now matches planted intent EXACTLY in every file (main 3, b 2, a/c 0) across all 6 languages. Real downstream ripple confirmed and re-baselined: apex c.cls state_mutation 3->1 (the manifest's own pre-fix note had already predicted this -- c's return was providing phantom branch context that #2546's x3 flux weighting amplified; removing return-as-branch removed the phantom trigger, leaving the raw hit).

kotlin's object declaration is the globals plant AND counts class_start (a.kt class_start 2) — a documented tier-1 exception to the no-classes tripwire, like cobol's PROGRAM-ID: object IS kotlin's singleton-class construct.

swift's _dependency_capture requires module names of 2+ characters ([a-zA-Z_][\w.]+), so 'import a' captures nothing: the corpus's swift chain never resolves, popularity stays 0, and no orphan->api conversion fires. Real single-letter modules are rare but the +-quantifier looks unintentional next to other languages' * shapes. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2543 (capture tail [\w.]+ -> [\w.]*): 'import a' captures, the swift chain resolves, orphan->api conversion fires (a/c api 0->3, b 1->4). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): scoped to `popularity|api`, the two the verdict pins.

go's safety_bypasses rule's dot-import alternation (\bimport\s+(?:\.[ \t]+)?") matches EVERY quoted import, not just dot-imports: +1 bypasses per importing file corpus-wide. The (?:\.[ \t]+)? being optional makes the dot-import detector fire on all imports. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2542 (dot made mandatory in the alternation): plain quoted imports no longer count, corpus go safety_bypasses main/a 1->0, b 3->2.

Languages whose visibility IS a naming/declaration convention count it wholesale: go's encapsulation rule counts every lowercase top-level symbol (7-9 per corpus file), perl's counts every my declaration (3-4 per file). Correct morphology, but cross-language encapsulation comparisons must expect these to run structurally hot.

typescript's args rule counts statement-position call parens (describe(kit), expect(kit)) in addition to declaration params — a.ts args 5 for 3 declarations (finditer-confirmed). Plants that are bare calls contaminate args in ts. Batch 4: apex and groovy count statement-position calls the same way (main args 7 = 4 sigs + 3 dispatch calls); objective-c over-counts via selector-colon segments (related morphology, recorded per-manifest).

m4 and scheme have _dependency_capture = None: include()/(import ...) count the import signal but can never produce a DAG edge, so popularity stays 0 and orphans never convert, corpus-wide. Two whole languages invisible to network_risk_sensor by construction — worth an upstream note whether deliberate. Batch 5: yacc (#include counted, capture None) and markdown (no import rule at all) join — four registry languages structurally invisible to the DAG. scheme RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2652 (added _dependency_capture handling both the corpus's bare (import a) form and real R7RS/Guile library-list forms) -- removed from languages_seen; m4/markdown/yacc remain. SCOPE CORRECTION (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): markdown REMOVED from languages_seen — the entry had it as "no import rule at all", but a None `import` rule is not a None `_dependency_capture`. markdown defines a live capture (the inline-link form `[text](target)`) and its DAG resolves: dependency_links 3, popularity 0.75, betweenness 0.0833, producer_ratio 0.5, i.e. the same values as python/fortran/swift. Its `import` cell is n/a (no rule), which is markdown-lit-plane-morphology's business, not this entry's. m4 and yacc remain, and the scan confirms the full pinned profile they share: dependency_links 0, dependency_density 0, popularity 0, betweenness 0, closeness 0, producer_ratio 0, pagerank at the uniform 1/N 0.2, normalized_blast_radius 200, api 0 (orphans never convert) and therefore risk_api_exposure 0.0 against a 5.29 median — that last one is the red cell this entry has to own, so the signal list names it. Batch C's C.3 removes m4/yacc once #2652's capture shape is extended to them.

Classification is per-file with no folder-context bleed: a .py file without its own micropython marker (import machine etc.) classifies as plain python even when every sibling is embedded — verified via the DB language column, twice (machine.idle() alone was NOT a sufficient discriminator; import machine was). Also two rule-level divergences on byte-similar code: embedded io drops os./sys. (python counts them), and orphan->api conversion does not fire under embedded classification. UPDATE 2026-08-31: the no-conversion divergence was fixed upstream by gitgalaxy#2548 (embedded_python never wired into Python-family indentation scoping — found independently by a tri-comparison sweep); orphan->api conversion now fires under embedded classification (api 6, verified by the CI gate's fresh scan against gitgalaxy main). The per-file classification and io-rule divergences still stand. First ledger entry re-baselined by an upstream fix — the GATING self-improvement loop closing end to end. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): `io|api` — the two measurable divergences (embedded's io rule drops the os./sys. prefixes python counts; orphan->api conversion, since fixed by gitgalaxy#2548). The per-file classification itself is not a metric and is not joined on.

dart's and zig's globals rules match final/const/var initializations at ANY indentation — function-local declarations count as globals (dart b/c +1 each from local finals; zig b 2 from function-local vars). Other languages' globals rules are top-level-anchored; these two look unanchored by accident. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2651 (anchored to true column 0 in both languages): dart b/c and zig b/c globals counts drop to the correct 0 for function-local declarations.

Collective entry for batch 4's finditer-confirmed dual-rule keywords, each detailed in its language's manifest notes: agc RESUME (cleanup+branch), livecode global (globals+bypasses) and throw (safety+branch) and then/end-if inflation, tcl source (import+io) and close (cleanup+io) and trap (safety+branch), dockerfile ENV (globals+state) and HEALTHCHECK (func+safety) and FROM (import+class_start), makefile clean-target (func+cleanup+api), matlab clear/clearvars (state+cleanup), m4 popdef (state+cleanup), apex Database.query (high_risk+bypasses), powershell trap/continue (branch duals). SCOPE CORRECTION (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the signal is now the union of the duals itemised above, and languages_seen is narrowed to the languages that actually carry one, because the reports join signal x language as a cross-product and a collective entry over languages with nothing itemised would mark their red cells explained. Removed: dart, groovy, objective-c, scala, scheme, zig — batch 4 swept them, but none records a dual-rule keyword in its manifest notes (groovy's args behaviour is ts-callparen-args; objective-c's selector over-count is the same entry). embedded_python is kept and its duals named: `except` is dual safety_bypasses+safety and its test plants overlap safety (assert-overlaps-safety-and-test family), which is why `test` is in the union.

html's func_start rule (<script>/<style> tags) never fires end-to-end: the polyglot splitter consumes the tags before html's rules run (micro-repro: <script>var x=1;</script> records the JS body's state signal on the html row but func 0; raw regex matches all 13 corpus tags, engine records 0). Rule passes direct-detector tests but is dead in production scans.

Collective entry for Tier-2 finditer/report-confirmed shapes, detailed per-manifest: css at-rules triple-count (func+branch, @supports also safety; args tracks @import url); jcl EXEC PGM= is high_risk per step (probes use EXEC <proc>), api appears only via orphan conversion (no api rule defined); yaml counts every name:/description: as doc and embeds shell inside run: strings; solidity SPDX line = ownership on every file; html meta author is dual doc+ownership. SCOPE CORRECTION (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): signal set to the union of the shapes itemised above (css func_start/branch/safety/args, jcl high_risk_execution/api, yaml doc, solidity ownership, html doc+ownership), and languages_seen narrowed to the five the verdict itemises. Removed: markdown and yacc — batch 5 swept them but recorded no shape here, and both are covered by their own entries (markdown-lit-plane-morphology, markdown-prose-is-doc-morphology; yacc-test-no-native-testing-concept, yacc-union-class-start-gap). Same cross-product reason as batch4-dual-keyword-overlaps.

Post-gitgalaxy#2610 (PR #2611: prism strips //* to the comment surface; jcl gains safety=COND=, safety_bypasses=COND=EVEN/ONLY, telemetry=MSGLEVEL=/MSGCLASS=, shared debt rules) the shell re-plants args 13 (PARM= per EXEC step), safety 2, safety_bypasses 2, telemetry 2, fragile/planned debt 1/1 -- all land exactly (report-confirmed 2026-08-31). Remaining zeros are intended morphology, not extraction gaps: cleanup deliberately has NO jcl rule because the honest idiom DISP=(...,DELETE) would double-count io's DISP= (decision recorded in gitgalaxy#2610); doc has no JCL doc-comment idiom distinct from //* comments; test has no JCL concept; globals has no scoped-vs-global distinction (JOBLIB/STEPLIB plants would inflate io + dependency_links). dependency_links 4 vs planted 3 = the DD DSN= capture on CORPUS.DATA -- deliberate blast-radius design (datasets ARE jcl dependencies), finditer-confirmed. comment_lines stays below median even with the comment surface live: JCL permits no blank lines and the metric (total_loc - coding_loc) counts other languages' blank-line style as comment mass. branch 3 / state_mutation 2 match planted intent exactly; their red/amber standing is inflation of the cross-language median by the #2545 return-in-branch family and #2546 flux weighting, and re-baselines when those land. 2026-09-01: the comment_lines clause of this entry is RESOLVED by gitgalaxy#2625 (PR #2632 + rosetta bias_report doc_loc switch): the metric now reads prism's real doc_loc, blank lines no longer count as documentation, and jcl sits at 11 vs median 12 (-8%, green).

cobol args 1 vs planted 13 is intended morphology, not an authoring gap (bucket-3 test run before ledgering, jcl PARM= precedent checked). (1) Paragraphs — the corpus's 12 probe functions — declare no parameters in COBOL; the language's only argument surface is the program-level PROCEDURE DIVISION USING (1 clause). (2) The file-level args metric counts rule MATCHES, not captured names — verified empirically 2026-08-31 by scanning a modified shell whose PROCEDURE DIVISION USING carried 13 parameter names: file_data.struct_args still records 1 (the per-function args_count path splits names, but the bias metric reads the file-level hit count). (3) Every construct that would add per-probe USING/RETURNING matches (CALL ... USING, ENTRY ... USING, INVOKE ... RETURNING) is ALSO an api-rule keyword (ENTRY|LINKAGE SECTION|CALL|INVOKE|EXPORT), so planting 12 of them would trade one red for api distortion — overlap-cost rejection, same precedent as jcl's DISP= cleanup decision (ledger jcl-2610-rebaseline-residual-morphology). GENERALISED 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the same shape — the corpus's function construct declaring no parameter list, with args matching an unrelated construct — was confirmed in css, dockerfile, html, makefile, sqlite, yacc and yaml, and now carries the cross-language entry args-no-parameter-surface-morphology, which also covers avg_func_args. This entry is kept for cobol's own two sub-findings (args counts rule MATCHES, not captured names; the api-overlap rejection) and for citation stability in data/cobol/expected_signals.json.

Guidestar manifest files carry no executable code, so the engine classifies their non-blank lines as doc_loc (package.json: total 8/coding 0/doc 7; pyproject.toml: doc 4). Only the 3 manifest-bearing corpus folders (javascript/python/rust, deliberate guidestar test design per #2557) inherit this extra doc mass; at the honest post-#2625 median of 12 real comment lines, javascript's +7 lands red (19, +58%) and python's +4 stays in-band (15, +25%). Verified 2026-09-01 by per-file doc_loc scans against engine pull/2632/head. Quirk noted for a possible future issue, not chased: rust's Cargo.toml produces NO file_data row at all (excluded before recording), while package.json and pyproject.toml are scanned and counted -- inconsistent manifest treatment across ecosystems.

markdown's entire prose content is its documentation surface: prism classifies the non-blank .md lines as doc_loc (34 across the 4 shells vs median 12, +183%). A documentation format measuring high on a documentation-mass metric is correct morphology, not bias. Verified 2026-09-01 per-file (a 8 / b 8 / c 7 / main 11) against engine pull/2632/head.

markdown is a markup format deliberately measured on the lit_* literary plane (engine markdown.py wires ONLY lit_code_blocks/lit_diagrams/lit_headers/lit_links; detector's #691 prose deflection routes the whole body to the doc surface, code payload stays empty). Reviewed all 18 absent-rule cells per GATING's n/a rule 1: none is a missing-rule gap. No callable units or control flow exist (func_start/args/class_start/branch -- lit_headers are the probe analogue, hence functions_found 0); io/state_mutation/globals/test/safety/safety_bypasses/high_risk_execution/telemetry/cleanup have no markdown idiom -- prose ABOUT those concepts is documentation, not executable signal (bucket-2 test fails: no construct a practitioner would defend as the language's own idiom); doc as a keyword rule would double-count the prose mass prism already routes to doc_loc (see markdown-prose-is-doc-morphology); planned_debt/fragile_debt keywords in prose are content, not code debt, and the empty code payload means the rules could never fire; ownership has no comment syntax to carry an author tag (HTML comments exist but are unplanted and rare as authorship idiom); import stays n/a because links are already counted on the lit plane (lit_links) AND now feed the DAG directly via _dependency_capture (gitgalaxy#2638) -- an import keyword rule would triple-count the same construct. keyword_hits (-45% amber) is the arithmetic shadow of the lit plane: only 4 lit rules can hit. SS3 risk metrics floor for a no-code language and are structurally incomparable (risk_documentation measures documentation OF code; with zero coding_loc the formula bottoms out at its constant terms) -- downstream, not chased, per the epic. dependency_links was the one real gap in this family and is FIXED upstream by gitgalaxy#2638 (relative links -> DAG edges: main->a->b->c resolves, import_count main/a/b=1 c=0, popularity a/b/c=1; api stays 0 since orphan->api conversion needs functions). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): `functions_found` and `avg_func_args` added to the signal list — the verdict already establishes both ("no callable units ... hence functions_found 0"), and markdown's avg_func_args 0.0 against a 1.0 median was the only red args-family cell in the corpus left with no entry naming it once args-no-parameter-surface-morphology took the other eight languages. The rest of the structural family (avg_func_loc, avg_func_complexity, gini, ...) is the 'downstream, not chased' set above and stays out.

AGC's real 1960s YUL/GAP instruction set (agc_assembly.py:99-101, comment: 'AGC lacks native objects') has no struct/record-defining pseudo-op -- its data/memory constructs (ERASABLE/FIXED MEMORY, EQUALS, 2DEC/2OCT, CADR/ECADR) are already fully covered by globals/memory_alloc/pointers. Contrast with the generic `assembly` entry (assembly.py:105-108), which DOES map class_start to struc/STRUCT/.struct macros -- proof the engine already detects struct pseudo-ops where they exist. AGC's narrower, real historical ISA genuinely has no equivalent directive; this is not an oversight relative to its sibling, it's a real capability gap between two different real assemblers.

GNU M4 is a pure text-substitution macro processor; neither M4 nor Autoconf (the corpus's real-world use case) has any record/object/type-declaration concept. func_start already covers macro definition (m4_define/AC_DEFUN); reviewing the full rules dict (m4.py) finds no other m4/autoconf idiom resembling a compound-type or entity boundary. Unlike yacc or fortran, there is no sibling 'macro processor with a type system' in the registry to suggest this is an engine gap rather than the language's actual shape.

GNU Make's model is variables plus file/phony targets; it has no entity or type-declaration concept. The one candidate construct, `define ... endef` (a named multi-line template), is already correctly wired to `macros` (makefile.py:216) rather than an object/entity boundary -- it defines a reusable text template, not a typed record, and double-wiring it to class_start would misrepresent it as an OOP-like boundary it isn't. No record/struct idiom exists anywhere in real Makefile usage.

Comment at shell.py:119-121: 'Shell is strictly procedural.' The one candidate construct, associative arrays (`declare -A`), is a data-structure instance, not a type/entity declaration, and isn't wired anywhere (pointers/immutability_locks/encapsulation cover declare -n/-r but not -A). Unlike tcl, which has real, idiomatic OOP frameworks (TclOO/Snit/Itcl, wired at tcl.py:70-72) precisely because tcl programmers commonly use them, there is no comparably common bash-native class convention in real-world scripts to anchor a rule to.

CSS is purely declarative with no embedded imperative/scripting payload, unlike the other languages that wire these three signals only against such payload: html's cleanup/telemetry fire on inline JS (removeEventListener/clearInterval, <script src=analytics>/sendBeacon); dockerfile's fire on shell build steps (apt-get clean, LOG_LEVEL); yaml's telemetry fires on GH Actions workflow commands (::debug/::warning/::error). CSS never carries any of that. cleanup: no destructor/teardown lifecycle exists -- rules are declaratively re-evaluated per paint; the closest analog (unset/initial/revert/revert-layer) is already claimed by panics_and_aborts, so a cleanup rule over the same tokens would double-count; clear:both is a layout primitive, not resource teardown. state_mutation: custom-property declarations and cascade overrides are declaration/specificity resolution, not temporal reassignment (no 'was A, now B' model) -- mirrors html's identical state_mutation=None/identical stated reasoning; css and html are the two purely-declarative languages in the taxonomy that null this signal while dockerfile/yaml (imperative-payload-bearing) wire it. telemetry: no logging/analytics primitive; scroll-driven-animation constructs are already captured by events/listeners. Corpus-confirmed: data/css/{b,c}.css's probe-state/probe-telemetry/probe-cleanup keyframes are empty placeholders -- bucket-3 test (could the shell plant something real?) fails for all three; nothing exists to author.

io stays None correctly, but css.py's inline comment gives the wrong reason ('url()/@import don't block a computational thread'); that doesn't hold against html's own io rule, which fires on non-blocking async fetches (src=/href=//

html has no native idiom for scoped-vs-global variables or state mutation -- it is purely declarative markup; both concepts are inherently imperative/scripting concepts that live in embedded JS. Micro-repro (window.myGlobal=1; document.getElementById(...).innerHTML=...; let y=2; inside a real <script> tag, committed scratch scan against engine main a837c3a): arch_globals=2, state_flux=1 on the html file row -- confirming these DO populate via the <script>/<style> HANDSHAKE_REGISTRY bucket-continuation (same mechanism ledger html-script-func-start-unreachable/gitgalaxy#2549 already documents for func_start) whenever a real <script> tag is present; a pure-markup file with no embedded script scores 0 for both, correctly, since html's own rules are None. The only candidate HTML-native constructs for globals (data-* config attributes on <html>/<body>, <meta> site config) are already fully claimed by the args rule (generic data-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+) and doc/api rules (meta name=.../property=...) -- overlap-cost test fails, same precedent as jcl's globals ledger entry ('no scoped-vs-global distinction'). The only candidate for state_mutation (<details open>/<dialog open> user-toggled state) is already claimed by the branch rule's <details|summary|noscript> match. No unclaimed construct a practitioner would defend as HTML's own idiom for either concept exists.

yacc.py's test rule is None. Bison's only assertion-shaped construct is %expect N / %expect-rr N (declared conflict counts), but the engine already claims those tokens inside internal_discriminator (yacc.py ~L48) purely for C-vs-yacc file routing, not as a measured signal -- and %expect is a single declarative pragma, not a repeatable per-case test idiom like pytest markers or Foundry's test*/assertEq (which solidity's own test rule captures). Embedded C action blocks are NOT routed through a separate C rule set: detector.py's Mode_A_Labels (~L2392, yacc has no entry in _lens_config.py's HANDSHAKE_REGISTRY) applies yacc's own rules over the whole rule body including its {..} actions, so a stray assert() in an action already lands under yacc's safety rule rather than going unmeasured. Corpus confirms this by construction: a.y's 'probe_test : TWO ;' is a deliberately action-less production (test: 0 planted) -- there is no way to write a genuine test idiom inside a .y grammar file that isn't either generic C already caught elsewhere or the routing-only %expect pragma. Real absence of morphology, not an engine gap.

solidity.py's io rule is None with an explicit comment ('EVM blockchains are closed systems'). Checked whether emit/event -- solidity's real observable-output idiom -- is folded into telemetry: it is not; telemetry is narrowly console.log (Hardhat debug only, L181). The actual destination is a dedicated events rule (emit|event, L168), reinforced by ipc_rpc_bridges (.call{value:, emit [A-Z]\w*, L224-226) for cross-contract calls, and globals (msg.sender/block.*, L110-112) for chain-context reads -- solidity's engine already gives io's real-world equivalents (outbound chain interaction, logging) first-class dedicated signals, more specific than a generic io bucket would be. main.sol's probeIo function is deliberately inert (return route; only) and expected_signals.json plants io:0 across every file, matching this being a deliberate design choice already partly self-documented in the corpus manifest notes ('io is undefined for solidity... counted under globals/ipc instead'). Real absence of morphology -- io-intent is already measured, just under more precise signal names (events/ipc_rpc_bridges/globals) rather than an engine gap.

yacc's class_start is None, but bison's %union { ... } directive declares a real compound type (the C union spanning every rule's semantic value) -- the exact shape the engine already maps to class_start for other non-OOP languages (fortran TYPE...END TYPE, cobol PROGRAM-ID/CLASS-ID, generic assembly struc/STRUCT). yacc.py's own internal_discriminator already lists union among its %-directive routing markers, but no signal rule counts it. 2/2 real crucible .y files (freebsd config.y, jailparse.y) use %union in the standard form. Engine gap, not real morphology; cell stays n/a until the rule lands, then the corpus can plant a %union probe (same choreography as jcl COND=/#2610).

html's high_risk_execution is None and the srcdoc attribute is invisible engine-wide: a file of just <iframe srcdoc="<script>eval(1)</script>"> scores state_danger=0 (micro-repro, committed scratch scan) because the JS handshake trigger requires ^[ \t]*<script starting a line (never fires inside a quoted attribute) and io's attribute list (src|href|action|poster|data) omits srcdoc; grep -rn srcdoc across the engine returns zero hits. The REST of html's inline attack surface is measured, just elsewhere: isolated probes show on[a-z]+= lands in listeners + reflection_metaprogramming and href="javascript:..." lands in safety_bypasses (no double-count wanted there). Engine gap for srcdoc specifically; cell stays n/a until the rule lands.

yaml's ownership is None, but the two ecosystems this language definition explicitly targets each carry a standard single-key ownership field: action.yml's top-level author: (sibling of name:/description:, which yaml's doc rule already matches) and OpenAPI's info.contact: block (openapi.yaml is a discriminator). Neither overlaps any current rule (checked doc/globals/state_mutation/import). Direct precedent: jcl's Author:|Maintainer: and dockerfile's MAINTAINER/LABEL maintainer= ownership rules. Engine gap; cell stays n/a until the rule lands.

yaml's cleanup is None. GitLab's after_script: is correctly excluded (already routed to func_start as an executable-logic anchor, test-asserted -- a cleanup rule over it would double-count, same rejection shape as jcl DISP=(...,DELETE)/#2610). The real gap: yaml's philosophy counts shell embedded in run:/script: like code (branch/io/high_risk_execution all reach into it), yet teardown verbs there are invisible to every signal -- rm -rf <non-root-path> (high_risk_execution's rm -rf is deliberately root-only, test-asserted), docker rm/stop/down (nothing), bare kill <pid> (panics_and_aborts only catches kill -N). Engine gap; cell stays n/a until the rule lands.

powershell's api rule's bare-identifier alternative lacked the keyword exclusions func_start/args already carry, so param(/if(/switch( lines miscounted as API surface -- RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2656 (same exclusion set added). main.ps1 api 6->0 (all 6 old raw matches were param()/switch(/if(, zero real API surface); a/b/c.ps1 6->3 (raw contribution drops to 0, the +3 orphan-conversion credit per file is unaffected).

lua's api rule's module-export 'return <ident>' alternative allowed any indentation, so ordinary function-body returns miscounted as module exports -- RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2657 (anchored to column 0). main.lua api 6->4, a/b/c.lua 8/9/9->6/6/6 (raw regex contribution drops to just the real function-declaration matches; orphan-conversion credit unaffected).

each language's doc rule included a bare AUTHOR/Author:/meta-name=author alternative that the ownership rule already owns exclusively, so every header author line double-counted doc+ownership -- RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2650 (abap) and gitgalaxy#2659 (agc_assembly, fortran, livecode, html). Each language's main file doc drops from 2 to the correct 1. cobol shares the identical pattern but was deliberately excluded (its shell has no other doc-idiom content, so the fix would drop doc to 0, not 1) -- tracked separately as gitgalaxy#2661, needs a corpus-side doc line planted first.

the doc rule matched opening and closing docstring delimiters independently with no pairing, so one docstring counted doc=2 -- RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2658 (matches the full delimited span as a single bounded non-greedy hit). Both languages' main file doc drops from 2 to the correct 1.

makefile had zero brace-delimited bodies but was missing from detector.py's Mode_A_Labels tuple, silently falling through to Mode_B_Braces and dropping ~100% of real functions -- RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2648 (added to the tuple, alongside ada). Corpus-wide effect: real function extraction now works, enabling orphan->api conversion (a/b/c.mk api 0/0/1 -> 3/3/5) and correcting b.mk's state_mutation (6->2, the x3 flux multiplier no longer phantom-fires once function boundaries are correctly recognized).

signal_processor.py's _get_locational_multipliers applies PATH_MODIFIERS (analysis_lens.py) by matching the file PATH, so the corpus's own layout and file names feed cross-language differences into the risk_* columns that no signal count explains. Micro-repro: SignalProcessor()._get_locational_multipliers('data/jcl/main.jcl') -> {'cog': 0.7, 'safety': 0.85}; 'data/c/a.c' -> {'safety': 0.85}. Survey over all 184 shell files (2026-09-02, engine 3ac91822): (1) 'data/' matches the data-directory rule -> safety x0.85 on EVERY file, uniform, no bias; (2) the 'config' rule (?:^|/)(?:configs?|settings|environments?|setup|makefile|\.env|cntl|jcl)\b matches the folder names data/jcl/ and data/makefile/ -> cognitive_load x0.70 on all 8 files of those two languages -- the only case where the corpus's folder NAME, not its content, moves a score; (3) the header/declaration extension rule (.h/.hpp/.hxx/.cpy) -> cog x0.85 on cobol a/b/c.cpy; (4) entry-point file-name rule on main.{c,cpp,go,java,js,py,rs,ts} -> dead_code x1.25 (main files of the other 38 languages are not matched); (5) markup/data extension rules zero a metric outright: css/html async x0.0 (concurrency), markdown doc x0.0, sqlite state_mutation x0.0. (2) is the actionable one for cross-language reading: jcl and makefile cognitive_load sits 30% low by construction. Deliberate engine behaviour for real repositories (config directories are declarative); recorded here so bias_report readers do not chase it as a rule or formula deviation. Found during the gitgalaxy#2655 design pass, whose identical-input grouping had to key on these multipliers before the evidence-mass floor's invariance showed as exactly 0.00. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the multiplier keys in the survey map to risk columns via signal_processor.py's assembly — cog -> risk_cognitive_load, safety/memory -> risk_safety_score, async -> risk_concurrency, state_mutation -> risk_state_flux, dead -> risk_dead_code, doc -> risk_documentation — and the signal field now names those six. The unexercised keys (debt, test, spec, secrets) are left out: no corpus path matched them in the 184-file survey.

perl's doc rule lists =cut in the same alternation as the POD openers and nothing pairs them, so a correctly closed POD block counts doc=2 (opener + =cut). Identical to the shape gitgalaxy#2658 fixed for python docstring delimiters. Differential micro-repro on data/perl/main.pl, engine main @3ac91822, full_precision: adding the single line '=cut' takes doc 1 -> 2 with every other recorded signal unchanged. The corpus previously read doc=1 only because its POD block was left UNTERMINATED, which was itself hiding a much larger effect: detector.py ~L3042 (the #2239 POD strip) blanks from a POD opener to the next =cut or, failing that, to end of file, so all of main.pl was invisible to the structural slicer -- avg_func_loc 0.0, avg_func_complexity 0.0, func_internal_density 0.0, structural_mass 104.52 against siblings' 8-11, and functions_found 9 against a 13 median. Closing the block restores all of them (6.75 / 0.75 / 0.111 / 11.9). doc=2 is baked in per GATING (the corpus measures what the engine does); filed as gitgalaxy#2670, to be folded into gitgalaxy#2669 B.1's doc-block family fix.

cobol's doc rule lists AUTHOR in the same bare-tag alternative that its ownership rule owns exclusively -- the shape gitgalaxy#2659 fixed for agc_assembly/fortran/livecode/html, from which cobol was deliberately excluded because its shell had NO other doc-idiom line: removing AUTHOR from doc would have taken doc to 0, not to the planted 1. gitgalaxy#2661 sequences the fix; this is step 1, corpus-side. main.cbl now carries a genuine structured doc line, '*> @return the probe result' (COBOL 2002+ inline form, already in cobol's doc rule), so doc reads 2 = AUTHOR. + *> @return until #2661 step 2 removes AUTHOR from the doc alternative, at which point it settles at the planted 1. Note cobol has no alternative ownership idiom -- its ownership rule matches ONLY 'AUTHOR.' -- so the corpus cannot dodge the collision by swapping the header the way apex could; doc 2 is unavoidable in the interim and is baked in per GATING.

The corpus's function construct takes no parameter list in these languages, so `args` and `avg_func_args` read low by morphology, not by an authoring gap. Shared criterion, applied per language against the live registry (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the construct the corpus counts as a function (the language's `func_start` rule) declares no parameters, and the `args` rule matches some *other* construct entirely, so SPEC's "each probe taking exactly one argument where the language expresses arguments" has nothing to attach to. Corpus-wide `args` totals against the 13 median: css 3, html 3, dockerfile 4, yacc 2, makefile 1, sqlite 1, cobol 1, yaml 0; `avg_func_args` is 0 or near-0 in all eight for the same reason (the hits that do exist are not inside probe bodies). Per language, with the plant-anyway option priced by running the candidate through the live compiled rules (finditer, same screening method as A.1): (css) probes are at-rules and an at-rule takes a condition, not a parameter list; the args rule matches CSS functional notation (calc|clamp|min|max|var|env|url|rgb...) inside declarations, and all 3 hits are the `url("a.css")` of the @import chain in main/a/b (c is the leaf) — i.e. args here is a byproduct of the planted `import`, the third arm of css-import-url-io-triple-overlap. `width: calc(1px + 1px)` would raise it to 13 at zero overlap cost and is DECLINED: a value expression in a declaration body is not the at-rule's parameter. (html) probes are `<script>`/`<style>` tags (themselves unreachable end-to-end, gitgalaxy#2549) and the args rule matches ATTRIBUTES (data-*, aria-*, name, value, for, ...); the 3 hits are a.html's two `data-testid` and main.html's `name="author"` ownership meta — byproducts of other plants. `<input name= value=>` also fires `api` (planted and scored); a bare `data-probe=` is clean apart from unscored structural_boundaries, and is DECLINED on the same ground: an attribute is not an argument to a callable. (yacc) probes are grammar rules and `$$`/`$n` semantic-value references are the nearest thing yacc has to a parameter surface, so this one is rejected on OVERLAP COST rather than absence: `probe_x: TOKEN { $$ = $1; }` scores args 2 AND state_mutation 1 (b.y's existing state 2 is exactly that assignment plus a counter++), so actions in the 12 productions would add 12 to a planted, scored column to move an unplanted one — the same trade cobol rejected. (yaml) probes are `run:` steps and the args rule matches a `with:` block, which in GitHub Actions binds to a `uses:` step and never to `run:` — unreachable from the corpus's function shape. Planting it costs a `uses:` line, which fires `import` AND `_dependency_capture`: fake edges in the planted main->a->b->c DAG (import = 3 corpus-wide) that the graph layer cross-checks. (makefile) probes are targets (extraction fixed by gitgalaxy#2648) and targets take no parameters; make's parameter surface is `define`/`$(call f,...)`/`$(1)`, and `define` matches the registry's `macros` rule, NOT `func_start` — converting probes to macros would delete 12 planted func_start occurrences — while `$(call ...)` additionally fires `reflection_metaprogramming`, a scored input to risk_cognitive_load. main.mk's single hit is its one `$(call probe_branch)` dispatch. (dockerfile) probes are RUN/CMD/HEALTHCHECK instructions, which take no parameters; `ARG` is a file-scoped build variable and the corpus already plants one per file (FLAG/ENVKIT/SHAPE/PLAN = 4). Nine more ARG lines are overlap-free (finditer: args only, no `globals` — unlike ENV, which is dual globals+state) and DECLINED: no instruction would consume them, so args would be measuring how many ARG lines someone typed. (sqlite) probes are CREATE INDEX statements (the #2513 tri-comparison precedent) and an index takes no parameters; args matches bind placeholders (?1, :name), `VALUES (...)` row constructors and CTE parameter lists, all of which live in DML — and every DML verb that can carry one (SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|REPLACE) is also an `io` keyword in sqlite's own rule, so each args plant costs +1 io, against a language whose io is already the batch's largest residual (#2669 B.4). main.sql's one hit is its `VALUES (1)`. (cobol) full verdict in cobol-args-clause-match-morphology (paragraphs declare no parameters; the only argument surface is the program-level PROCEDURE DIVISION USING; every per-probe alternative is also an `api` keyword); listed here so the shape is one entry and so `avg_func_args` is covered, which that entry's args-only signal did not reach. NOT in this entry, deliberately: agc_assembly. Its args rule matches register-target operands (\b(CA|CS|TS|AD|SU|...)[ \t]+(A|Q|L|Z)\b) and the AGC calling convention really does pass an argument in the accumulator, so it HAS a parameter surface; #2669 A.3 planted `CA A` at each probe entry and took args 2 -> 13, avg_func_args 0.167 -> 1.0 (the median). Resolved by authoring, not morphology — A.4's item list was written against the pre-A bias_data cache and still named it. markdown is likewise absent: its args rule is None, so the cell is n/a rather than low (markdown-lit-plane-morphology).

apex's import rule is compiled with re.IGNORECASE, which neutralises the [A-Z] guard in its second alternative (\b[a-zA-Z_]\w*\.[A-Z]\w*\b), so the alternative degrades from "lowercase receiver, capitalised member" — a type reference — to "any word.word", and every qualified method call counts as an import.
